correctness.rationale: At 0<c<1, any served buyer can profitably drop out and any unserved nonbuyer can profitably buy. The reverse also holds: with no nominations to buyers and all nonbuyers served, changes of the nominations of a continuing buyer do not raise that buyer's payoff, and neither changing buy to abstain nor the reverse benefits the deviator. Thus fixing q nonbuyers leaves an ordered (by purchaser labels) list of k-subsets covering the nonbuyers. The necessary q≥k and k(n−q)≥q are sufficient by the cyclic assignment, also when only one purchaser fits the model. Inclusion–exclusion over omitted nonbuyers with the factor C(n,q) counts precisely these profiles. Independently, write L=log n and B=kn log n−kn log L−n log(k!). At q0=floor(n/L), the probability of a missed recipient is at most q0 exp(−k(n−q0)/q0)=O(n^(1−k)/L), which tends to zero even at k=1. The logarithm of C(n,q0) is o(n), and log C(q0,k)=k log q0−log(k!)+O(1/q0); together these give log N(q0)=B−kn+o(n). The relaxed upper bound g_n at a n/L for fixed a>0 is B+kn(log a−a)+o(n). Its strictly decreasing derivative, positive at a=1−ε and negative at a=1+ε for large n, places every exterior value below the larger endpoint bound. Relative to q0 the endpoints lose kn(a−1−log a)+o(n), a positive linear loss; summing over at most n counts proves convergence in probability. Equilibrium coverage and the extremal feasible counts give both cost ratios. A covering optimum uses at least ceil(n/(k+1)) buyers and the cyclic construction attains it; dropping coverage cannot improve the welfare optimum when an unserved player can instead buy for c<1.
residual_risks: The concentration proof is for fixed k and for the uniform measure over labelled nomination profiles. The supporting finite enumeration concerns only the exact count and equilibrium characterization, not the asymptotic.

evidence: For k=1, the census is exactly C(n,q) q! S(n−q,q) by the classic Stirling onto-map identity. For k>1, the counted objects are bipartite incidence lists with every purchaser row of weight k and every recipient column positive, disallowing repetitions within each row.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A prior enumeration and concentration for these weighted bipartite lists under the same sampling would count as coverage. The known onto-map count covers the one-choice combinatorial slice, not the arbitrary fixed row-weight asymptotic.

originality.rationale: The best-response structure and extremal welfare calculation are antecedents, as is the Stirling/surjection form of the count when k=1. The inclusion–exclusion itself is standard. The supported increment is the specified full labelled PNE census together with concentration at n/log n nonbuyers for general fixed k, not a new price-of-anarchy result or novelty for the classical k=1 combinatorics. The strongest model and asymptotic analogues do not give that distribution.
residual_risks: The Stirling asymptotic papers referenced by DLMF were not individually inspected for the binomially weighted k=1 limit, and no originality judgment on that isolated slice is needed.
Ranked catalogue and primary-literature comparisons cannot exclude a result on the full incidence-list distribution under another parametrization.

value.rationale: Knowing which equilibrium sizes exist or that an inefficient equilibrium exists does not tell whether inefficiency is exceptional under the stated counting measure. The result shows that uniformly counted profiles typically incur almost the worst cost for that n and identifies the sublinear scale of the missing purchases. This supplies a quantitative multiplicity result distinct from extremal inefficiency, without treating the uniform measure as a behavioral prediction.
residual_risks: No equilibrium selection mechanism is modeled, and the probability statement does not extend directly to increasing k or different network families.
